title: Cadrora - guided Windows setup
welcome:
I'll guide you through your first sign-in.

1. Connect your GitHub fork and choose your profile.
2. Prepare Cloudflare with the pages and instructions you need.
3. Save your profile and enable automatic publication.
4. Open your website and sign in.

Your answers are saved. Use the same installation name to resume.
accountStep:
STEP 1 OF 5 - Sign in to Cloudflare

Cloudflare will host your website and photos.
1. Sign in, or create an account and verify your email.
2. Choose the account for this website using the account menu at the top left.
3. Copy the URL from your browser's address bar, then paste it directly below and press Enter.
domainStep:
STEP 2 OF 5 - Connect your website address

Your website address: {0}

If your domain is listed as Active, press Enter.
Otherwise:
1. Click Add domain (sometimes Onboard a domain). Enter the main domain you bought, such as example.com.
2. Choose a plan. The Free plan works for this setup.
3. Check that Cloudflare has kept your existing website and email records.
4. Follow its instructions to change nameservers at the company where you bought your domain. Nameservers tell the internet where to find your domain.

Wait until Cloudflare shows Active. This can take time: type stop and return later if needed.
You do not need to create a website DNS record; the installer handles that. If you do not own a domain yet, buy one first.
tokenStep:
STEP 3 OF 5 - Allow the installer to set up your website

The page opening now prepares five permission rows and selects your account. It does not create a key yet.
1. Add Account > Vectorize > Edit and Account > Turnstile > Read.
2. Check that all seven rows below are present. Add any missing rows with Add more:
   Account > Workers Scripts > Edit
   Account > D1 > Edit
   Account > Workers R2 Storage > Edit
   Account > Vectorize > Edit
   Account > Turnstile > Read
   Zone > Zone > Read
   Zone > Workers Routes > Edit
3. Under Account Resources, select only your website's account.
4. Under Zone Resources, change All zones to Include > Specific zone and select only your domain.
5. Click Continue to summary, then Create Token. Copy the key; Cloudflare shows it only once.

If no form opens, click Create Token > Create Custom Token and use the same rows.
Paste the key directly below, then press Enter. Input is hidden. The key is saved encrypted on this computer and reused when you restart the installer.
r2Step:
STEP 4 OF 5 - Enable photo storage

Cloudflare calls its file storage R2.
1. If you see a list of buckets (storage folders), it is ready. Press Enter.
2. Otherwise, choose Get started with R2. Review the payment details and possible charges, then activate it if you agree.
3. Wait for the bucket list, then return here and press Enter.

The installer creates the storage folders for you. Leave any existing folders alone.
turnstileStep:
STEP 5 OF 5 - Protect your sign-in page

Turnstile checks that people signing in are not bots.
1. Click Add widget manually (sometimes Add widget).
2. Name it Cadrora {1}.
3. Under Hostnames, add: {0}
4. Keep Managed selected. Leave Skip future security rule challenges off.
5. Click Create, then Integrate the widget yourself if offered.

Keep this page open. I'll ask for its Site key and Secret key next.
If you already have a widget for this website, use that one. Do not rotate its secret.

firstLogin:
Let's sign in to your new website
1. Type password below to open your private password file, or open it yourself:
{0}
2. Copy only the value after ADMIN_PASSWORD= and save it in your password manager. Do not change the file.
3. On the sign-in page opening now, paste that password and finish the security check. This is your website password, not your Cloudflare password.
4. When you see your website's admin dashboard, return here and press Enter.

If sign-in fails, type stop. On your next run, -ReplaceToken changes your Cloudflare API key; type keys at a failed Turnstile check to replace those keys. Your first sign-in remains unfinished until you confirm it.
